  • Tuya (NYSE: TUYA) reported Q3 2026 earnings per share of $0.03, matching estimates.
  • Revenue of $98.6 million exceeded estimates and rose 19.5% year-over-year.
  • The board approved a cash dividend of $0.057 per share.

Tuya (NYSE: TUYA) provides platform-as-a-service offerings, AI applications, and smart home and robot products. It reports third-quarter 2026 earnings per share of $0.03, matching the $0.03 estimate. Revenue of $98.6 million exceeds the $95.8 million estimate.

Revenue rises 19.5% from $82.5 million a year earlier, as highlighted by PRNewsWire. Founder and CEO Jerry Wang calls it Tuya’s 13th consecutive quarter of year-over-year revenue growth and says growth accelerates from the second quarter. Shipments in AI-related product categories rise more than 400% from a year earlier, as highlighted by MarketBeat.

Platform-as-a-service revenue rises 18.3% to $70.1 million. AI application and other revenue rises 18.6% to $13.6 million, while smart home and robot product revenue rises 26.7% to $15.0 million, as highlighted by PRNewsWire.

Overall gross margin falls 2.5 percentage points to 45.8%, while platform-as-a-service gross margin declines to 45.7% from 48.8%. Operating margin rises 4.4 percentage points to 9.0%, as highlighted by PRNewsWire.

Tuya’s board approves a cash dividend of $0.057 per ordinary share and per American depositary share, totaling approximately $35 million. Co-founder and CFO Alex Yang says this marks its third consecutive fiscal year of paying a dividend.

  • Best Buy (NYSE: BBY) is set to release its fiscal third-quarter 2027 earnings on November 24, 2026.
  • Wall Street anticipates earnings of $1.49 per share and revenue of $9.89 billion.
  • The company is focused on increasing profit margins, with a new CEO potentially signaling strategic shifts.

Retailer Best Buy (NYSE: BBY) is scheduled to report fiscal third-quarter 2027 earnings before the market opens on Tuesday, November 24, 2026. Wall Street estimates earnings of $1.49 per share and revenue of $9.89 billion. The company also plans to discuss the results on a conference call.

A separate consensus estimate puts earnings at $1.48 per share for the quarter ended October 2026, up 5.7% year over year, and revenue at $9.84 billion, up 1.7%, as highlighted by Zacks Investment Research. That earnings estimate is down 0.3% over the past 30 days.

Best Buy is working to increase profit margins, while its new CEO could signal a change in strategy. Second-quarter adjusted earnings per share rose by a double-digit percentage, while revenue grew more modestly. Analysts expect relatively modest third-quarter improvements, as highlighted by The Motley Fool, which also reports that shares are down 1.33%.

Best Buy’s annual dividend yield is 3.92%, with a quarterly dividend of $0.96 per share, or $3.84 annually, as highlighted by Benzinga. At the share price used in its calculation, about 1,563 shares worth approximately $153,096.00 would generate $6,000.00 a year in dividends. Income and yield can change with payments and the stock price.

Best Buy trades at a trailing price-to-earnings ratio of 16.11 and a price-to-sales ratio of 0.48. Its trailing earnings yield is 6.21%, debt-to-equity ratio is 1.30, and current ratio is 1.12.
